predecessors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
predecessors.text: Kannauj (Kanyakubja), occupied after the Gurjara-Pratihara descendants of Devapala were destroyed

successors.name: Ghurid dynasty
successors.text: the Gahadavala realm: the Ghurids defeated Jayachandra at Chandawar in 1194 and sacked Varanasi

ledger.x: c. 1085: Chandradeva founds the Gahadavala kingdom at Varanasi. The page has him 'established a sovereign kingdom sometime before 1090, after the decline of the Kalachuri power' and 'declared independence sometime before 1089 CE'; 'Chandradeva likely captured this…

c. 1100 (bridge): the land between the three named centres joins. The 1100 Chandrawati inscription is the last dated attestation of Chandradeva's kingdom and the page puts the furthest north-west inscription at Rahin in Etawah district; no page names any other town, border or conquest. Cliopatria…
by 1109: Govindachandra, then prince, wins Kannauj back.
1120: Kalachuri land between the Yamuna and the Sone.

c. 1124 (bridge): Govindachandra holds part of Bihar. 'In the east, Govindachandra controlled a part of the present-day Bihar' and 'His easternmost inscription has been found at Maner in Patna district'; 'In the north-east, his kingdom was probably bounded by the Burhi Gandak River'. The page does…
1140s: the Pala-Gahadavala conflict revives over western Bihar.
1152: Cliopatria's shape trims 24 cells (and adds 16) against 1085.

c. 1155: the Bihar contest ends with the reign. Govindachandra 'controlled part of present-day Bihar, but lost the eastern territory by the end of his reign' (his last inscription is of 1154; the list has c. 1155). The year is the end of the reign (confidence 1).

c. 1155: the Bihar land is lost. 'However, the Pala inscriptions in this area indicate that he lost this territory by the end of his reign', 'this territory' being the part of Bihar he controlled; Munger 'later came under the control of…
1194: the Gahadavala kingdom ends at Chandawar.

wars.name: Gahadavala-Ghaznavid wars
wars.outcome: The Ghaznavids take Kannauj between 1104 and 1105 and hold Madanapala to ransom; Govindachandra restores Gahadavala power there by 1109 and a peace treaty follows; Vijayachandra repulses a Ghaznavid invasion 'sometime before 1164'.

wars.name: Pala-Gahadavala wars
wars.outcome: The Palas invade before 1109, possibly in revenge for Chandradeva's expansion; the conflict 'revived in the 1140s CE over western Bihar'; Govindachandra possibly reaches Munger c.

wars.name: Govindachandra's Kalachuri war
wars.outcome: Kalachuri land between the Yamuna and the Sone is annexed; Kalachuri titles adopted in 1120.

wars.name: Sena-Gahadavala conflicts
wars.outcome: Infobox line only; under Vijayachandra 'the Sena invasion came from the neglected eastern border' (Gahadavala page).

wars.name: Battle of Chandawar
wars.outcome: Jayachandra is defeated and killed; the Ghurids sack Varanasi; Harishchandra holds a rump to 1197 (list) and the dynasty ends under the Delhi Sultanate.

certainty.note: No boundary on either page except the Burhi Gandak (north-east) and the Yamuna-Sone region; the Bihar frontier with the Palas and the Himalayan rim are approximate.
